title: Pilot: Precision Profiles and Prompt-Gating Field Notebook
content:
Context and intent:

This notebook captures the field experiments and playbook notes from the Acme Health pilot (masked) where we trialed a lightweight prompt-gating classifier + model-routing policy to reduce cost while preserving clinical QA quality. Goal: keep 95th percentile latency < 420ms for interactive flows, reduce token spend by ~35% vs naive 13B baseline, and avoid regression in F1 on our eval set (medical-qa-small v2).

High-level architecture tested:
- Front door: request arrives -> simple cost/latency header extraction -> prompt-gating step (fast classifier) -> route to model variant and quant profile -> run inference -> post-process (reranker/cleanup).
- Prompt-gating classifier: distilled 125M classifier (onnx int8) that estimates "complexity score" (0-1) and returns labels: trivial, routine, complex. Runs on CPU with 12ms median.

Why prompt-gating?
- Many customer inputs are short lookups or template-based requests where a small model + prompt rewriting yields identical UX but at much lower cost.
- Allows aggressive quantization and smaller models for trivial/routine traffic while preserving a high‑quality model for complex queries.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Models: Mistral-7B (float16 baseline), Llama2-13B (float16 baseline for quality comparison), Llama2-7B-FT (task-adapted, small tuning), and a Redwood-verified 13B distilled variant (rdw-13b-dist).
- Quant profiles: fp16, int8 (GPTQ-style), awq-4bit, awq-3bit-aggressive (edge case).
- Routing policies: always-high, naive-size (route by length threshold), prompt-gating (classifier-driven), random-canary (5%).
- Prompts/pipelines: direct prompt, prompt + constrained-prefix-cache, prompt + reranker (cheap embed match then model for disambiguation).

Key empirical findings (short):
- Classifier accuracy: complexity classifier precision on complex class = 0.92, recall = 0.88 on our 1.2k holdout examples. Failure modes: long context with short question (classifier underestimates).
- Latency: end-to-end median latencies by route (on Dedicated A100-equivalent): trivial->mistral-7b-awq-3bit = 110ms median, routine->mistral-7b-int8 = 160ms, complex->rdw-13b-fp16 = 380ms.
- Throughput: batch size 8 continuous: trivial path achieved 380 tokens/s; complex path ~95 tokens/s.
- Cost savings: estimated token spend reduction 32-38% vs routing all to 13B fp16 baseline (varies by traffic mixture).
- Quality: overall F1 drop across customer eval set was -0.7 absolute (baseline 0.842 -> 0.835) for prompt-gating routing with conservative thresholds. Aggressive awq-3bit on routine flows caused -2.1 absolute regression in routine-narrow QA cases; reverted those to int8.

Prompting heuristics discovered:
- For template-ish inputs (detected by regex /forms|DOB|policy|claim-id/), a small rewrite to canonical form before classification improves classifier recall for trivial class by +7 points.
- Use of a 1-2 shot micro-context for routine medical lookup prompts (cite few typical Q/A) reduces hallucination rate on small models by ~40% while adding ~15 tokens. Cost tradeoff acceptable on routine flows.
- Cacheable prefix segments: questions that share the same patient metadata header benefit from prefix KV cache. We saw 20% token reduction on average for multi-turn triage flows.

Decision log (practical actions taken during pilot):
- 2025-11-18: Start pilot with conservative thresholds -> gate trivial->mistral-7b-int8, routine->l2-7b-ft-int8, complex->rdw-13b-fp16. Rationale: avoid early quality hits.
- 2025-12-03: Observed slight uptick in complex misclassifications for longer context questions. Implemented heuristic: if input_length_tokens > 360 then force complex route.
- 2025-12-14: awq-3bit caused regression on certain differential-diagnosis style prompts. Rolled back awq-3bit for routine; retained for trivial short templated prompts only.
- 2026-01-09: Canary expansion to 15% traffic for prompt-gating; no customer incidents reported. Tracked per-customer error rates separately.

Operational/playbook notes:
- Canary & rollbacks: 1) Start with 2% of traffic, 2) monitor latency, QA F1 on sampling pipeline, 3) bump to 5% -> 15% -> full. If QA F1 delta > 1.5 or latency SLO violation count > 0.5% then rollback.
- Observability hooks needed: per-route token counts, per-request classifier decision, route latency, downstream model version, post-check failure reason. Add quick label in trace metadata: route_reason=[classifier|length|regex|manual].
- Alerting: set regression alert when sampled F1 drops > 1.0 for 1 hour or customer error rate increases > 0.3%.

Engineering constraints & tuning knobs:
- Classifier: keep under 20ms p95; if classifier latency spikes (p95 > 40ms) we fall back to length-based route to avoid cascade.
- Model warm pools: maintain 2 warm instances of rdw-13b in Dedicated pool to keep cold-start outliers < 50ms added overhead. Consider per-customer pinning for high-volume customers.
- Cache composition: prefix cache TTL 45s worked well for triage flows. Longer TTL caused staleness for dynamic patient context.
- Batch sizing: routine pool tuned to batch 6-12. Trivial pool benefits from batch 16-32 but watch latency SLO.

Unresolved questions and next steps:
- How to automatically tune classifier thresholds per-customer? Initial thought: use small continuous eval that samples labeled traffic to calibrate. Need infra for per-customer sampler + retraining cadence.
- Explore using an embedding-based pre-check for similarity to cached responses (cheap vector check) before invoking any model. Latency budget ~10ms — viable on CPU? Need microbench.
- Revisit AWQ-3bit: can we restrict to a narrower prompt shape automatically (detect templated form)? Work with research to craft a shape signature.

Quick checklist before moving to broader pilot (for SE/FE):
- [ ] Add classifier decision trace field to Trace API (ticket SE-8240).
- [ ] Add per-route token billing breakdown in Console (product ticket Product-514).
- [ ] Implement length-forcing heuristic as configurable flag.
- [ ] Add sampled QA-eval pipeline to collect per-route F1 in nearreal-time (infra task INF-332).
- [ ] Finalize rollback policy + playbook and share with CS and SRE.

Appendix: representative prompt templates used during experiments (kept short):
- Templated lookup (trivial): "Patient DOB: {{dob}}
Question: What is the next scheduled vaccine?"
- Routine triage (routine): "Presenting symptoms: {{symptoms}}
What are likely differential diagnoses and next steps? Keep answer concise and cite guidelines."
- Complex consult (complex): "Full history and note follows: {{long_history}}
Synthesize the likely diagnosis and list follow-up tests and differential, explain uncertainty."

Notes to self:
- Customer very concerned about hallucinations in med domain — tradeoffs need conservative safety floor.
- Keep snapshots of seed prompts and exact model versions in linked artifacts.

If we proceed: propose 8-week staged rollout plan (detailed timeline in linked confluence).
